A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SPE-BR pricing study. Their main text, equations, figures and complete appendices are readable, and relocated proofs and illustrations can be matched reliably.

before.justification: V2 Section 7 and Figure 2 report original simulations measuring estimation errors, equilibrium convergence and cumulative regret.

after.justification: V3 Section 6 and Appendix J report original simulations, including contraction sensitivity and unequal-exploration experiments in Figures 5–7.

M1.justification: The two-stage estimation and best-response procedure remains. V3 adds an exploration-split selection rule in Equation (14), used in Appendix J, whereas v2 leaves the split as an input. V3 Equation (11) also explicitly imposes monotonicity on the implemented link estimator, unlike v2's displayed optimization.

E1.justification: Synthetic pricing with N=2,4,6 sellers remains; v2's setup and plot labels establish N=6 despite its erroneous N=8 caption. V3 Appendix J.1 adds an environment with unequal exploration periods, exposing sellers to mixed random and adaptive competitor prices during estimation.

E2.justification: Neither version empirically evaluates competing pricing algorithms. Both assess SPE-BR against true parameters, equilibrium prices and the hindsight revenue benchmark. Comparisons with cited learning methods remain theoretical.

E3.justification: The simulations change from links Φ(u−i+1) to Φ(2u/i), introduce three sensitivity settings per seller count, and replace horizons {100,200,400,800,1600} with {100,400,800,1600,3200}. Appendix J.1 introduces randomized seller-specific exploration lengths. V3 specifies uniform noise on [−0.05,0.05]; v2's printed noise bounds are malformed, preventing an exact noise comparison.

E4.justification: Beyond v2's convergence curves across seller counts, v3 adds sensitivity tests for contraction constants near 0, 0.5 and 1, fitted log-log rate analyses, and robustness tests violating common exploration timing. These investigate convergence mechanisms and the consequences of dependent exploration data.

E5.justification: Reported independent simulation repetitions decrease from 35 in v2 Section 7 to 30 in v3 Section 6 and Appendix J. Both retain averages and 95% confidence intervals.

E6.justification: V2 Figure 2's results are replaced by the expanded, differently configured results in v3 Figures 5–6, with additional unequal-exploration outcomes in Figure 7. V3 reports synchronized regret slopes of 0.54–0.71 and unequal-exploration slopes of 0.72, 0.67 and 0.65 for N=2,4,6. These are newly reported results, not same-setting performance improvements.

T1.justification: V3 replaces v2's quadratic-growth assumption with uniform strong concavity, removes the interior-equilibrium requirement, and introduces projected best responses and Lemma 3.3. The main bounds change from N^(1/2) to N^(3/2), with revised error aggregation in Appendix G. New derivations establish local monotonicity of the surrogate demand function and characterize the exploration split; much of the general shape-constrained regression proof is retained.

C1.justification: The contribution summary materially weakens the claimed multi-seller scaling: regret changes from approximately N^(1/2)T^(5/7) to N^(3/2)T^(5/7), and price-convergence dependence changes from N^(1/4) to N^(3/4). The headline time exponents and the broad semiparametric pricing contribution remain unchanged.

C2.justification: V3 adds substantive explanations connecting equilibrium uniqueness, contraction and estimation error, and interprets unequal-exploration errors through non-i.i.d. prices while emphasizing robust pricing performance. It adds an efficient-solver limitation and removes v2 Remark 4.7's argument that noncontractive markets are unrealistic. Its new claim that convergence accelerates as the contraction constant approaches one conflicts with Equation (9) and several Figure 6 slopes.

D1.justification: V3 specifies the exploration coefficient, split-rule constants, sensitivity grid and Gaussian sampling parameters in Appendix J, and explicitly summarizes sellers' known and unknown information in Appendix A. Its reproducibility statement replaces v2's repository link with supplementary ZIP and notebook execution instructions. These substantially expand documentation, although the stated archive's availability cannot be verified from the PDFs.

R1.justification: V3 adds the hotel-pricing service example, references including Friesz et al., Scutari et al. and Tsekrekos and Yannacopoulos, and an explicit monopolistic-rate comparison with Fan et al. It removes the Cooper et al. discussion and several references, while retaining the principal positioning relative to Li et al. and Balabdaoui et al.

P1.justification: The introduction and related work are extensively condensed and rewritten. V3 introduces a three-step equilibrium narrative, moves formal estimation results and explanatory remarks into Appendices D and I, integrates general notation into the preceding section, and replaces the concluding recap with a focused future-directions section.

P2.justification: V3 replaces the original experimental display with multiple-condition curves, confidence bands and log-log plots, adds an unequal-exploration schematic and three tables, and places experimental figures in the appendices. V2's policy schematic survives as Figure 8, while its three proof illustrations survive as Figures 1–3; these are relocations rather than new content.

improvement.justification: V3 adds useful robustness evidence, improves reproducibility documentation and corrects the omitted seller factor in error aggregation. However, after dropping the interior-equilibrium restriction, its revised Appendix G assigns the wrong sign to the first-order term at a constrained revenue maximum, leaving boundary-case regret reasoning unsupported. New Lemma 3.3 also asserts equilibrium uniqueness from individual strong concavity alone. These concerns affect central guarantees, so the documented benefits do not establish a reliable net quality improvement.
